The data, and how it connects

Every source, every file, every column — with real rows out of the bucket. Companion to Graph Technical Reference, which covers what happens to this data once it is read.

49 sources · 432 CSV files · 93,505 documents · bucket moine-data

1. What a scraper is

One folder per source under scrape/, holding a manifest.yaml and the code to fetch. The manifest is the contract — the runner reads it, nothing else hardcodes a source.

scrape/<Category>/<site>/
    manifest.yaml     name, s3_base, enabled, schedule
    scrape.py         fetch, normalise, write CSV

enabled is the switch. A disabled source is skipped entirely: it is not fetched, it publishes nothing, and so it triggers nothing downstream. Every source is disabled unless deliberately turned on.

What a run does

1  fetch          the source's API, bulk file or pages
2  normalise      into CSV with a stable header
3  stage          write under _runs/<run_id>/
4  commit         copy to the source's stable path
                  rewrite _LATEST.json
5  emit dataset   Dataset("s3://moine-data/<s3_base>")
A commit replaces, it does not append. Each source publishes a full snapshot at a stable key, overwritten each run. ClinicalTrials.gov holds exactly two objects: a 2.9 GB CSV and _LATEST.json. This is what makes double-counting structurally impossible — there is no incremental append to get wrong, and a rebuild from the same snapshot yields the same counts. Two consecutive builds on 2026-07-30 both produced exactly 1,049,701 ClinicalTrial nodes.

The cost of that choice is that the lake keeps no history: _LATEST.json records only the current run, so the gap between two scrapes cannot be recovered after the fact.

2. How the two stores stay in step

Step 5 above is the whole mechanism. A commit emits an Airflow Dataset, and the two sync DAGs are subscribed to datasets rather than to a clock.

@weekly --> scrapers_pipeline
              commit task emits Dataset("s3://moine-data/<s3_base>")
                   |
                   +--> graph_sync          35 CSV-publishing sources
                   |      build  ~24 min --> validate --> import ~8 min
                   |
                   +--> vector_store_sync    8 document sources
                          chunk --> embed --> upsert to Qdrant

Neither sync DAG has a schedule of its own. They wake when data lands, so a sync cannot race the scrape that feeds it, and a week where nothing publishes costs nothing.

Both use DatasetAny. A plain list of datasets means AND in Airflow — the DAG would wait for every listed dataset. For graph_sync that means firing only when all 35 sources publish in one window, which is to say never, and silently.

graph_sync's trigger set is derived from graph/sources.py at DAG-parse time rather than listed, so declaring a new file there updates the trigger with nothing to keep in step by hand.

Rebuild, not update

The graph is not patched in place. Every sync rebuilds the whole graph from the current snapshots, validates it, and replaces the store. neo4j-admin database import has no transaction — it writes a fresh store — so the validator is what stands between a bad build and a live graph that answers confidently and wrongly.

The vector store is incremental, because re-embedding 93,000 documents costs hours on GPU. Ingest compares each S3 object's ETag against what is indexed and touches only what changed; chunk IDs are deterministic, so re-ingesting a known document overwrites in place instead of duplicating.

3. The graph schema

Generated by graph/make_schema_png.py. 22 node labels, 32 relationship types.

4. The lake

Eight categories. A source lives in exactly one, and its s3_base is <Category>/<site>/.

Of the 49 sources, 35 feed the graph (77 declared files) and 8 publish documents to the vector store. Three — ema, mhra, pmda — do both, so 40 sources are used and 9 are not. Exclusions are recorded with reasons in graph/sources.py and repeated against each file below.

5. Every source, every file

Columns are the real header. Rows are the first records of the real file, transposed so wide files stay readable; long values are cut at 90 characters.

Clinical Trials Pipeline Intelligence

Trial registries. Nine of them, deliberately overlapping: the same study is often registered in two places, and the second registration carries the sponsor or the enrolment the first one omitted.

Likely pathogenicPathogenicPathogenicPathogenicPathogenicUncertain significance
Dec 17, 2024-Jun 29, 2010Jun 25, 2024Jun 29, 2010Jun 29, 2015
This change likely results in a nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. It is not present in gnomAD v2.1.1 and was previously observed in individuals with complicated spastic paraplegia (reported in ClinVar). It was identified in an affected individual with macular dystrophy, without extraocular features.
